title: Psychometric Order-Effect Audit of Preference Annotation by LLM Judges

original_idea.body:
# Order-Effect Audit of LLM Judge Preference Annotation

**Problem:** LLM judges exhibit anchoring and order effects, so preference data may be systematically biased.

**Direction:** Present response pairs in both orders and with anchoring primes, measure position bias and label-flip rate.

**Why it matters:** AI preference data may silently carry cognitive biases at scale. Pure inference.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2502.04134; arXiv:2503.10229; arXiv:2412.03605.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Judge bias corrupting preference data is real but chain to catastrophic risk is moderate.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pure inference order/anchoring swaps on an open judge; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: position/anchoring measurement with label-flip rate.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open judges, no lab data; independent-friendly fuzzy-reward auditing.

novelty.reasoning: LLM-judge position/order bias is well documented.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: LLM-judge position/order bias is extensively documented.
